title: A Metabolism-Driven Prognostic Model and PSMD14-SP1-GYS1 Axis Reveal Therapeutic Vulnerabilities in Melanoma.
authors: Xie, Jiaheng; Zhao, Songyun; Wu, Dan; Ma, Chenfeng; Yan, Wei; Zhang, Pengpeng; Lu, Qingyu; Wan, Zeyu; Tang, Qikai; Li, Liqun; Wang, Ming; He, Yucang
one_liner_zh: 该文构建黑色素瘤代谢预后模型并解析PSMD14-SP1-GYS1调控轴，虽涉及SP1转录因子与DNA结合，但核心为临床预后与湿实验机制，无AI/物理模拟的蛋白-DNA互作建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Melanoma is a highly aggressive cutaneous malignancy characterized by a strong propensity for metastasis and therapy resistance, with its progression being closely linked to metabolic reprogramming. This study integrated multiomics data (The Cancer Genome Atlas, Gene Expression Omnibus, European Nucleotide Archive) and advanced machine learning to develop prognostic and immunotherapy prediction models for melanoma, focusing on 114 metabolism-related pathways. Cox regression identified 70 genes linked to survival, with functional enrichment revealing key metabolic pathway alterations. A metabolism-related prognostic model (MRPM) was constructed using 101 combinations of machine learning algorithms, demonstrating superior predictive accuracy across 4 cohorts. High-risk patients showed worse survival and immunotherapy response in melanoma and other cancers. Tumor microenvironment analysis revealed MRPM's negative correlation with immune infiltration and positive association with tumor purity. Single-cell sequencing highlighted MRPM gene enrichment in melanocytes. Mechanistically, GYS1 (the key gene in MRPM) emerged as a pivotal prognostic gene that promotes melanoma proliferation and metastasis. Regulatory studies uncovered SP1's transcriptional control of GYS1- and PSMD14-mediated stabilization of SP1 through K48-linked ubiquitination removal. In vivo validation confirmed that PSMD14 knockdown suppressed tumor growth through SP1-GYS1 axis disruption. This work establishes MRPM as a robust predictive tool and elucidates the PSMD14-SP1-GYS1 regulatory network as a potential therapeutic target in melanoma metabolism.
abstract_zh: 黑色素瘤是一种高度侵袭性的皮肤恶性肿瘤，以强烈的转移倾向和治疗耐药性为特征，其进展与代谢重编程密切相关。本研究整合了多组学数据（癌症基因组图谱、基因表达综合数据库、欧洲核苷酸档案）和先进的机器学习方法，开发了针对黑色素瘤的预后和免疫治疗预测模型，重点关注114条代谢相关通路。Cox回归识别出70个与生存相关的基因，功能富集分析揭示了关键的代谢通路改变。利用101种机器学习算法组合构建了代谢相关预后模型（MRPM），在4个队列中展现出优越的预测准确性。高风险患者在黑色素瘤及其他癌症中表现出较差的生存率和免疫治疗反应。肿瘤微环境分析显示，MRPM与免疫浸润呈负相关，与肿瘤纯度呈正相关。单细胞测序突出显示了MRPM基因在黑色素细胞中的富集。机制上，GYS1（MRPM中的关键基因）被确认为促进黑色素瘤增殖和转移的关键预后基因。调控研究揭示了SP1对GYS1的转录控制，以及PSMD14通过去除K48连接的泛素化来稳定SP1。体内验证证实，PSMD14敲低通过破坏SP1-GYS1轴抑制了肿瘤生长。本研究确立了MRPM作为稳健的预测工具，并阐明了PSMD14-SP1-GYS1调控网络作为黑色素瘤代谢中潜在治疗靶点的作用。
